issue.title: react: Server side rendering can break when you use code that yields (node-fibers)
issue.body:
This is similar to this https://github.com/meteor/meteor/issues/10279

doing server side rendering (`ReactDom.renderToString`) with meteor and react >= 16.5 can throw an error:

```
Cannot read property 'debugElementStack' of undefined
```

This happens if two renderes start at the same time and if your App contains code that yield because of fibers.

## Background

In ReactDom server we have this piece of code:

```
pushCurrentDebugStack(this.stack);
try {
    out += this.render(child, frame.context, frame.domNamespace);
    } finally {
    popCurrentDebugStack();
}
```

`pushCurrentDebugStack` and `popCurrentDebugStack` both operate on a global array.

In a normal JS environment, this is no problem, because the three statements above always happen in this order:

// first render
`pushCurrentDebugStack`--> `this.render`--> `popCurrentDebugStack`
// second render
`pushCurrentDebugStack`--> `this.render`--> `popCurrentDebugStack`

If you have co-routines like fiber however, and in particular, if you use Collections or other fiber-yielding functions during `this.render`, `this.render` itself can yield and the order is no longer guaranteed, because the second render might start before the first finishes. This will lead to inconsistency.

## But isn't that a reactdom problem that should be fixed there?

Well... relying on the execution order like that is usually fine. They could fix it, by check which object to push and pop, instead relying on the order of execution. Could be an easy fix. But why should they fix it? They say:

> React supports standard-compliant JavaScript environments, so using an environment with non-compliant concurrency primitives is going to cause problems.

That's bad news for us, because it basically says that react does not support environments like meteor where we can have co-routines.

## Who is affected by that?

You will only run into this problem if 

- you render your app on the server (SSR, obviously)
- you use meteor-collections inside your render-functions (your `<App />`) or other fiber-yielding functions

So people using graphql/apollo or similar are not affected, because they have usually no yielding functions in their react-tree.

## Ok, the above error seems only to happen on develop. should i care?

This is not the only place where node-fibers and react-dom-server do not play nice together, see also this https://github.com/meteor/meteor/issues/10279

And we might have more errors like that in the future as long as meteor uses node-fibers or as long as react does not support such environments.


## What should we do?

i think we can't get rid of fibers easily, also in my opinion, it was a good tool when designing the old data-layer around pub/sub. It's also worth noting that SSR with meteor works quite well in general.

So our only chance is to get react to support it better, but that will also need some effort from the core-maintainers of meteor. At least in a way, so that we can monkey-patching situations like that (the fix usually is to attach globals to `require('fibers').current).
